text:
alex: Kicked off the handoff for the new asia-east1 GPU cluster. Bootstrapped nodes, installed drivers, added to autoscaling group. Ready for SRE ownership handoff when you are.

marta: Thanks. Can you drop the pager/alerting config and the quick validation checklist here?

alex: Sure — high level: PD policy `PD-asia-gpu-primary` (pd://policy/PD-asia-gpu-primary), Slack channel `#asia-gpu-oncall`, rotation: weekdays Ryan + Jordan, weekends Sam.

alex: Alerts shipped to PD: GPU_utilization_high (90% for 10m), GPU_memory_pressure (>=85% for 5m), Node_Readiness_Failed (>2 nodes), Pod_OOM_kill_rate (>3 in 15m), KubeEvictionRate (>0.5% 10m).

alex: Example alert rule (Prometheus):
```
alert: GPUUtilHigh
expr: sum by(instance)(nvidia_gpu_utilization_percent) / count by(instance)(1) > 90
for: 10m
labels: {severity: "sev2", team: "infra"}
```

jordan: Where are the escalation paths? primary -> secondary -> infra-lead?

alex: Yes. Escalation: 1) oncall (PD-asia-gpu-primary) 2) secondary (PD-asia-gpu-secondary) 3) infra-lead (ryan) -> exec pager if unresolved 2 hours. Add oncall runbook link in case timeline unclear.

alex: Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/asia-east1-gpu (internal) — contains boot logs, kube checks, and rollback steps.

sam: For paging noise: we set aggregated alerts for small blips and added a 5m burn-in window for util spikes. Also added annotation `suppress: autoscaling` for known scheduled scale events.

marta: Ownership: who owns capacity provisioning vs. cluster infra?

alex: DevInfra owns cluster infra (drivers, node images, autoscaler config). SRE owns service-level health, alert tuning, on-call response and cross-region failover. For capacity requests, product teams request via capacity-ops and we coordinate reservation.

ryan: Training and handoff checklist: 1) run the quick validation (below) 2) confirm PD routing + escalation contacts 3) verify dashboards + alerting in Grafana 4) run a simulated failover (node drain) 5) join the 30m walk-through w/ DevInfra.

alex: Quick validation commands:
```
kubectl get nodes -l cloud=asia-east1 -o wide
kubectl top nodes | grep gpu
kubectl get pods -n gpu-workloads --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
watch nvidia-smi -q -d UTILIZATION
```

alex: Known network caveats: inter-region egress to us-west has 100ms baseline; keep model-weights sync off-peak. VPC firewall: allow 10.10.0.0/16 for monitoring, 172.16.0.0/12 for inter-node.

jordan: Cost controls? any autoscale limits or spot fallback policies?

sam: Autoscaler max nodes set to 120 for now, min 8. Spot fallback allowed up to 40% of capacity with `safe_spot_profile` to avoid eviction-sensitive workloads. Logging retention for debug mode is 14 days by default to limit cost.

marta: If an oncall person gets an alert and can't resolve, how do they escalate to infra-lead? PD escalation step?

alex: Use PD escalation button -> calls infra-lead immediately. Also PM-staffed escalation channel `#infra-escalations` as backup. Documented in runbook section "Escalation contacts".

oncall-bot: Reminder: Scheduled walk-through with DevInfra tomorrow 09:30 PT. RSVP with :thumbsup: in the thread.

ryan: I'll lead the 30m session. agenda: topology, alerts, runbook walkthrough, one simulated node failure.

marta: I joined, will take first-week observation shifts and tune alerts.

jordan: Tested node drain simulation earlier — pods migrated cleanly, kube-proxy had a 30s flapping hiccup that recovered. Added a note to runbook to watch kube-proxy restart count.

alex: Good catch. Added to runbook: "Post-drain: check kube-proxy restarts > 3 -> investigate CNI version mismatch."

sam: FYI costing alert email sent to finance: projected monthly GPU spend ~ $95k if steady-state at 80% util. We'll monitor first 2 weeks for anomalies.

marta: Anything else before formal handoff?

alex: Last bits: PD policy ids: primary `PD-asia-gpu-primary`, secondary `PD-asia-gpu-secondary`. Slack channel `#asia-gpu-oncall`. Runbook link again: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/asia-east1-gpu. Handoff checklist marked complete in Ops tracker.

jordan: ACK — taking first weekday oncall.

sam: ACK — weekend coverage noted.

ryan: Officially assigning SRE ownership to the eng-sre rota. I'll update the org doc.

alex: Thanks all, closing handoff thread. :white_check_mark:

marta: :thumbsup:
